grants.title: Center of Gravity — Short-Term Scientific Missions
grants.funder: Center of Gravity / Niels Bohr Institute / Albert Einstein Institute
grants.eligibility: Research visit to be developed jointly with a Center of Gravity member; visit must begin after April 2027 and finish before 1 October 2027. Application conditions and available support are specified in the official call.
grants.relevance: Useful for initiating a focused collaboration on effective geodesic dynamics, black-hole phenomenology, or gravitational theory, if an appropriate host scientist agrees. This is a short visit grant, not a salaried academic post.
grants.notes: Deadline taken from the dated Albert Einstein Institute announcement. Funding call, not a location-restricted job.

grants.title: DFG Heisenberg Programme
grants.eligibility: Researchers qualified for a professorship by habilitation or equivalent track record; full professors abroad and holders of permanent W2/W3-equivalent roles are excluded. Applications accepted on a rolling basis.
grants.relevance: A potentially valuable route to pursue q-desics and SER quantisation independently at a German host institution. Your previous Associate Professor appointment abroad requires checking the exact nature and level of that role with DFG.
grants.notes: Ongoing programme, not a newly announced call. No fixed application deadline.

grants.title: DFG Reinhart Koselleck Projects
grants.eligibility: Outstanding researchers who hold or are eligible to hold professorships. German institutional integration and DFG applicant eligibility must be clarified; visiting affiliation by itself is generally insufficient. Rolling submissions.
grants.relevance: Could support a genuinely high-risk theoretical extension of q-desics or the quantum geometry programme if the proposal clearly lies outside standard DFG funding routes.
grants.notes: Five years, €500,000–€1.25 million. Ongoing programme, no fixed deadline.

grants.title: FWF Principal Investigator Projects
grants.eligibility: Qualified principal investigator and an Austrian host research institution with infrastructure; subject to the current FWF institutional work-time and research-focus conditions. Rolling submissions.
grants.relevance: A strong programme for a focused theoretical project computing quantum-geometric expectation values in SER quantisation and translating them into observable q-desic corrections.
grants.notes: Projects up to 48 months; this is an ongoing funding route, not a newly advertised call.

prospects.title: John Templeton Foundation — Mathematical & Physical Sciences (2027 watchlist)
prospects.country: International · eligible nonprofit research host required
prospects.eligibility: 2026 OFI deadline was 15 July 2026. The Foundation has not announced its 2027 MPS guidelines or submission window. It generally funds charitable institutions internationally rather than individual researchers or for-profit entities. The 2026 MPS round required a substantive experimental or observational project targeting BSM physics or technosignatures, with significant AI/ML methodology.
prospects.relevance: A potential 2027 direction combining SER-based quantum geometry, q-desic predictions, theory-informed AI/ML, and a concrete precision gravitational observation or experimental data-analysis programme. The planned collaboration with an AI/ML group at the Marietta Blau Institute strengthens the methodological fit, but observational/experimental BSM eligibility must be assessed against the new 2027 call.
prospects.notes: Strategic prospect ONLY; this is not an open call. Monitor both the 2027 MPS guidelines and the Intelligence Venture if the research advances AI methodology, rather than merely applying existing AI tools. Do not count as an active grant.
